items.title: Byron Stripling interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 25, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Sweets Edison told me, he says, “You know when I used to walk by white women I would always look at my shoes

ctx.x: Human nature is scary sometimes and I wonder how we change — what has to change first, the attitude or is it something that just has to be legislated? That you can’t get away with acting like that anymore.

I think — I like your language of legislating but it’s interesting I was working with a friend of mine that’s a lawyer. I had gotten this contract for a gig and it had all this crazy language in it about what I was supposed to do. And he goes, “It appears they don’t trust you.” He said, “And you can’t write trust in a contract.” The things that you and I are talking about now, they can’t be legislated or put in a contract. They have to come from the heart. And as we’ve talked about this being a problem, you have…

Maybe it’s the news that I choose to watch and the polls, but it seems like the majority of the country now feels like that. And it’s a minority that’s keeping the country down and with terrible intentions.
